title: Seventy-three per cent of Melbourne apartments built since 2019 provided exactly the legal minimum number of car spaces
oneLiner: If most buildings sit at the floor, the floor is binding.
body: Grattan found that since 2019, 73 per cent of Melbourne apartments and 70 per cent of townhouses were built with precisely the minimum parking the rules required. A rule that most projects would exceed anyway would not show this pattern; one that most projects would undercut if allowed does.
contextBackground: This answers the claim that minimums rarely bind because developers build parking anyway: in Melbourne they build to the line and no further.
contextDisagreement: Developers say building to the minimum reflects the rule setting market expectations, not suppressed demand for less; Grattan reads it the other way.

evidenceItems.citation: Grattan Institute, Wasted space, May 2026 — share of dwellings built at the minimum

otherClaim.title: Developers still build parking where buyers want it; minimums only bind where demand is below the mandate

claimItself.title: Developers still build parking where buyers want it; minimums only bind where demand is below the mandate
claimItself.oneLiner: A minimum changes nothing where people want cars, and forces waste where they do not.
claimItself.body: In car-dependent suburbs, apartments without parking do not sell, so developers build it whether or not it is required. The minimum only has an effect where buyers would accept less parking than the rule demands, which is exactly where it is most costly and least useful.

ownArguments.label: AGAINST
ownArguments.text: Seventy-three per cent of Melbourne apartments built since 2019 provided exactly the legal minimum number of car spaces

usedIn.relationSentence: This claim contradicts “Developers still build parking where buyers want it; minimums only bind where demand is below the mandate”

strengthDefinitions.decisive: It defeats the parent claim if accepted.
strengthDefinitions.relevant: It counts against the parent claim without settling it.
strengthDefinitions.tangential: True perhaps, but it does not land against this claim.
